1. Make the server listen on all interfaces

Inside a container, localhost / 127.0.0.1 can’t be reached from outside, so the server has to bind to 0.0.0.0. Check server.py for where it starts and make it look like one of these:

python
# Flask
app.run(host="0.0.0.0", port=8100)

# FastAPI / uvicorn
uvicorn.run(app, host="0.0.0.0", port=8100)

# Built-in http.server
HTTPServer(("0.0.0.0", 8100), Handler).serve_forever()

Add a Dockerfile (no file extension) in C:\searoute
dockerfile
FROM python:3.12-slim
WORKDIR /app
COPY requirements.txt .
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt
COPY . .
EXPOSE 8100
CMD ["python", "server.py"]

Also add a .dockerignore so local junk stays out of the image:

__pycache__/
*.pyc
.git/
venv/
.venv/
4. Test on Windows (needs Docker Desktop)
powershell
cd C:\searoute
docker build -t searoute .
docker run -d -p 8100:8100 --name searoute searoute

cd searoute
docker build -t searoute .
docker run -d -p 8100:8100 --restart unless-stopped --name searoute searoute
